entry.gap: Volume V is an extract: Schedules 7 (deductions), 9 (indexation), 11 (Project Company defaults) and 12 (termination compensation), the Direct Agreement and the omitted clauses (including those defining Notice to Proceed and Force Majeure Event) are referred to but not issued, yet the Note to Bidders deems any deviation not listed in Form 4-E accepted.
entry.already_settled: ADD-02 Q12 refers Bidders to 31.2, under which deductions are uncapped; ADD-01 Q6 confirms the payment is availability based. Neither supplies the missing Schedules.
entry.practical_impact: The Availability Payment in Form 4-F and the Financial Model depend on Schedule 9 (index series, base date) and Schedule 7 (deduction levels); termination sums and lender cure rights (Schedules 11-12, Direct Agreement) drive financing terms. Form 4-E cannot list deviations to terms not seen, yet unlisted deviations are deemed accepted.
entry.proposed_question: Volume V, Note to Bidders, page 2: The extract refers to Schedules 7, 9, 11 and 12 and to the Direct Agreement (Clauses 29.2, 31.2, 39.1, 39.5 and 40.1, pages 3-4), none of which has been issued, and states that a deviation not listed in Form 4-E will be taken as accepted. Will the Authority issue these Schedules and the Direct Agreement or, if not, does the deemed acceptance in the Note to Bidders apply only to the clauses reproduced in the extract?
entry.interim_handling: Build the Financial Model on the reproduced terms (60% CPI / 40% fixed indexation per 29.2; uncapped deductions per 31.2) and record the index and deduction inputs as assumptions in the financing-assumptions schedule, not as price conditions (VOL-I 10.5). Legal decides whether to record a reservation on the unseen Schedules in Form 4-E; nothing is assumed about their content.
